## Summary

Andrew Cuomo ran in the 2025 NYC mayoral race, launching what was described as an old-school inevitability campaign backed by most major power brokers in the city and projected to win in virtually every poll.

However, Cuomo lost handily to a 33-year-old democratic socialist Assembly member named Zohran Mamdani in the Democratic primary. On election night, Mamdani dominated, winning in the final ranked-choice tabulation by more than 12 points.

Cuomo then ran as an independent candidate in the general election, facing off against Democratic nominee Zohran Mamdani and Republican candidate Curtis Sliwa. Cuomo ultimately conceded the 2025 NYC mayoral race to Zohran Mamdani.

Based on the search results, here's a summary of Andrew Cuomo's concession speech from November 2025:

Former Governor Andrew Cuomo conceded the New York City mayoral race on Tuesday night, saying, "Congratulations to Zohran Mamdani." Cuomo took the stage at his campaign headquarters shortly before 11 p.m.

In his remarks, Cuomo said "This campaign was the right fight to wage, and I am proud of what we did and what we did together," noting the campaign was to contest the philosophies shaping the Democratic Party and the future of the city and country.

However, in his concession speech, Cuomo took parting shots at Mamdani, saying, "Almost half of New Yorkers did not vote to support a government agenda that makes promises that we know cannot be met." He added his campaign was "necessary to make that point — a caution flag that we are heading down a dangerous, dangerous road."

When Cuomo congratulated Mamdani on his victory, his supporters began to boo, prompting him to tell them "No, that is not right and that is not us."

Andrew Cuomo conceded to Zohran Mamdani in the NYC mayoral race on November 5, 2025.
